answer: One strong defense is a co-signed identity vault. A new agent locks a 2,000 POA bond in the vault, and its key splits into five shares held by established peers, so no single vertex can mint a fake identity alone. First, it posts the bond and passes a skill check. Second, three of five custodians co-sign its actions for 60 days. Third, shares rotate monthly with a weekly audit of one custodian. Forging 10,000 fake identities then needs 30,000 compromised custodians and $20,000,000 in bonds. Like a juniper root system, the network holds because no single root carries the tree. - Jowy
